mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10Y-2Y < 0) within the next 6 months, or GDP growth decelerates in the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the ISM Manufacturing PMI crosses above 55, it signals strong manufacturing activity and increased demand for raw materials, which will drive up input costs and squeeze corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in >60% of 20-day windows following PMI > 55, or PMI remains elevated above 55 for >6 consecutive months without causing a bear market.

mechanism_narrative: When the 2-year Treasury yield rises by more than 50 basis points in a month, it signals a rapid tightening of financial conditions that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive on the day following >50bps 2Y yield spikes in >50% of instances, or the Fed cuts rates within 3 months of the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4%, it signals a tight labor market that will drive up wage costs and squeeze corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in >60% of 20-day windows following UNRATE < 4%, or UNRATE remains below 4% for >6 consecutive months without causing a bear market.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts growth accelerates by more than 20% year-over-year, it signals over-exuberance in the housing market that will lead to a demand-side recession and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in >50% of 60-day windows following HOUST acceleration > 20%, or a recession does not occur within 12 months of the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the ISM Manufacturing PMI and the Bloomberg Commodity Index both rise by more than 10% in a month, it signals a surge in input costs that will squeeze corporate profit margins and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in >60% of 20-day windows following joint PMI/BCOM > 10% spikes, or the cost shock does not lead to a >50bps rise in headline CPI within 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the 10-year Treasury yield rises by more than 100 basis points in a month, it signals a rapid rise in borrowing costs that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, especially if the Fed is already in a tightening cycle.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive on the day following >100bps 10Y yield spikes in >50% of instances during Fed tightening cycles, or the Fed cuts rates within 3 months of the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4% and the employment cost index rises by more than 3% year-over-year, it signals a tight labor market with rapidly rising wage costs that will squeeze corporate profit margins and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in >60% of 20-day windows following UNRATE < 4% and ECI > 3% YoY, or the wage cost shock does not lead to a >50bps rise in core PCE inflation within 6 months.
